one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-08. Scheduled and verified at source: AT&T Q3 results before the open on Wed 2026-10-21 [45]; Verizon Q3 results Mon 2026-10-26 [44]; TMUS Q3 results ~4:05pm ET Wed 2026-10-28, call 4:30pm [40]. TMUS pre-guided Q3 soft (~250K postpaid account adds vs ~304K Street at the time, temporarily higher churn from the legacy-plan migration) [38], so a weak headline is largely known; Q2 already showed 277K adds and 0.99% account churn [2]. The read-across from AT&T and Verizon five to seven days earlier matters most in my lane: Verizon is guiding to the upper half of 750K-1.0M phone adds [28], so another strong incumbent print plus cable line adds would feed the share-loss narrative, while stable industry churn would ease it. The stock fell 13.27% on 2026-10-09 [6] on the SpaceX/800 MHz news, with VZ and T also down sharply [33], so the event is a sector shock whose service impact is years away (D2D 5G targeted 1H28 [36]); short-term reversal argues for a slight upward lean, but more FCC/SpaceX headlines and a 10-year at 5.22% [42] cut the other way. I did not verify the FOMC date or an FCC agenda item myself, so neither is weighted. Net: median ~$149.5, monthly vol ~11% (above 33%/3.5 = 9.4% because of three telecom prints in the window and post-shock volatility). Unchanged from round 1, since the supervisor's findings concern 12-month value, not the next month.

fair_value.method: Value at 2027-10-09 (ex the ~$4.7 of dividends paid in between). Blend of P/E 45% (horizon NTM EPS $14.99 x 11.25x = $168.6), EV/EBITDA 30% (company basis: 6.49x x horizon LTM Core Adj. EBITDA $38.9B = $252.1B EV, less $87.56B net debt incl. towers, over 1,012M shares = $162.6) and FCF yield 25% (horizon LTM AFCF $19.06B / 1,012M = $18.83 at 11.5% = $163.7): 0.45 x 168.6 + 0.30 x 162.6 + 0.25 x 163.7 = $165.6, rounded $166.

0.23 x $14.44 + 0.77 x $16.17 = $15.77 (Oct-Dec 2027 is ~23% of the next twelve months).

bear.story: Industry repricing. Cable keeps adding ~850K lines a quarter between Comcast and Charter on free-line and switching offers [31,30], Verizon and AT&T keep strong phone adds [28,29], SpaceX gets FCC approval and bids in the April-2027 upper C-band auction [35], and the market prices share loss. TMUS cuts the $40-41B 2027 EBITDA target [4] and NTM EPS falls to ~$14.5 on an 8x multiple (VZ is 8.23x today [8]) = ~$116, at my thesis-break level.

base.story: The legacy-plan migration lifts ARPA after a Q3 churn blip [38]. 2026 guidance is met and the 2027 framework is roughly delivered (EBITDA ~$39-40B) [4,5]. Starlink Mobile stays a 2028 story with coverage-not-capacity spectrum (79 MHz vs 280-380 MHz per carrier; 5G service 1H28) [36] and a $50-130B build bill [35], so the overhang caps the multiple near 10.5x NTM EPS of ~$15 = ~$158, a little below the $166 fair value.

bull.story: Satellite fears fade as Q3-Q4 industry prints show stable churn and incumbents pull back on subsidies [28,39]. TMUS delivers the 2027 targets in full with a 2028 outlook, consensus NTM EPS holds near $15.8 with no haircut, and the multiple re-rates to ~12.8x (still below TU's 15.5x and VOD's 13.6x) = ~$203. No Deutsche Telekom transaction is assumed: that rests only on secondhand press [43].

comps_summary.peer_range: Medians use the 8 core peers (VZ, T, CMCSA, RCI, BCE, TU, AMX, VOD). Fwd P/E 5.9x (CMCSA) to 15.5x (TU); EV/EBITDA 4.6x (CMCSA) to 9.7x (TU). The ev_ebitda_fwd field holds StockAnalysis TRAILING EV/EBITDA for every peer, because forward EV/EBITDA was not available from a free source; my EV method therefore applies a trailing multiple to horizon-LTM EBITDA. There are fewer than 10 peers in the median because only a handful of listed companies sell US-style postpaid wireless at scale: CHTR (distressed 2.34x) and DTEGY (consolidates TMUS) are listed but excluded. With all 10 the medians would be 9.91x / 6.91x.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: P/E 11.25x vs 9.95x median (+13%, about the 70th percentile, between AMX 10.9x and VOD 13.6x; below TMUS's 11.82x today). EV/EBITDA 7.6x on the StockAnalysis basis vs 7.38x median (+3%; TMUS 8.06x today), applied as 6.49x on the company basis. FCF yield 11.5% vs VZ 12.44% and T 11.62%.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The premium rests on growth visible in reported and verified numbers, not on sell-side outperform calls: TMUS Q2-26 service revenue +9%, postpaid service revenue +13% and Core EBITDA +12% [1], against Verizon guiding mobility and broadband service revenue +2.5-3.0% for 2026 [28]; a 3Y EPS growth forecast of 17.03% vs VZ 6.99% and T 11.06%, with PEG 0.67 vs 1.13 and 0.88 [6,8,10]; and a 2027 target framework maintained on 2026-09-03 [4,5]. I cut it from round 1's +21% to +13% because AMX trades at 10.9x on comparable growth [22], part of TMUS EPS growth comes from buybacks, and the growth gap is exactly what cable [30,31] and SpaceX [33-36] contest within the horizon. On EV/EBITDA and FCF yield I give almost no premium for the same reason.

thesis_break_reason: $115 is 7.96x the verified FY2027 consensus EPS of $14.44 [7], below Verizon's 8.23x [8], and a ~15.8% FCF yield on the low end of the 2027 AFCF target ($19.5B / 1,072.7M shares = $18.18) [4,3]. A sustained trade there would mean the market has abandoned both TMUS's growth premium and its 2027 framework: a cut to the $40-41B EBITDA / $19.5-20.5B AFCF targets, account adds well below the 950K-1.05M 2026 guide after the Q3 churn bump [1], or evidence that the industry is in a price war (cable and SpaceX taking share by price). It is ~23% below spot, about 0.8 sigma at 33% vol, so ordinary volatility rarely reaches it.

reasoning: Lane: industry. Round 2 revisions follow the supervisor's checks, each re-verified at source. (1) Company 2027 targets ($40-41B Core EBITDA, $19.5-20.5B AFCF, Feb-2026 8-K [4]) are maintained (Sept 3 8-K [5]), so I anchor on them with an explicit 1.5% haircut ($39.4B) instead of round 1's unexplained $38.8B. (2) The StockAnalysis net debt of $117.6B includes ~$29.1B of operating leases [2,6], which double-counted against post-lease Core EBITDA. I moved to the company basis ($84.10B + $3.46B towers [2]) and converted the peer multiple with TMUS's own basis ratio (1.172). (3) The share count was rebuilt from the verified authorization ($8.53B left at Jul 17) and the ~$30B framework: 1,012M. (4) The peer median drops CHTR (distressed) and DTEGY (circular): 9.95x / 7.38x. I trimmed the P/E premium to +13% (11.25x) but did not go to the supervisor's 11.0x, because the verified 17.03% vs 6.99%/11.06% growth gap and the 0.67 vs 1.13 PEG support a little more. Unlike round 1, the P/E is applied to horizon NTM EPS. (5) The DT holding-company bull case is removed from all numbers (secondhand press only). (6) Keyed (Alpha Vantage) and mirror (StockTitan, MarketBeat) sources were replaced by sec.gov and verizon.com. Fair value: P/E $168.6 (45%), EV/EBITDA $162.6 (30%), FCF yield $163.7 (25%) = $166, unchanged in level but rebuilt. Industry evidence is unchanged: incumbents recovered (VZ 184K phone adds [28], AT&T [29]), cable takes ~850K lines a quarter [30,31], and the SpaceX 800 MHz deal is coverage rather than capacity, with service in 1H28 [34-36], so it is a multiple overhang within the horizon rather than a P&L hit. Scenarios $116 / $158 / $203 at 27/52/21% (mean ~$156). The bull case fell from $215 to $203 without DT and the bear rose slightly. The ladder is a mixture of lognormals (sigma 0.25/0.17/0.17; overall log-sd ~0.28) with fattened extreme tails: median ~$157, P(>=149) = 0.58. The base case stays below fair value because the overhang and 5%+ yields [42] likely persist and 12-month momentum is strongly negative (-34%) [6]. Analyst targets (avg $241.5 [7]) are far above my range and given no weight beyond context. Research limits: sec.gov refused a generic scripted User-Agent, so filings were read with WebFetch; AT&T's own newsroom returned 403, so the AT&T date comes from a syndicated copy of its release.
